sara: quick followup on the transpose-scaling runtime semantics after the RFC. we left a few open questions around when to apply scale factors and which rounding strategy should be the default. want to capture a concrete decision here so the runtime + kv cache contract is unambiguous.

anya: saw drift in the canary when we delayed scaling until after transpose (post-scale). small but consistent bias accumulates in attention logits for longctx.

michael: two orthogonal choices: (1) apply scaling before transpose (pre-scale) so integer math sees already-scaled values, or (2) keep raw integer layout and apply scaling after transpose (post-scale). pre-scale tends to be numerically cleaner but may force copies when strides mismatch. post-scale keeps layout stable but can introduce bias in some operator orderings.

kevin: rounding mode matters too. stochastic rounding reduces low-bit bias but breaks determinism and adds overhead. nearest-even is fast and reproducible. bankers rounding is another option but less common on HW.

anya: concrete canary data: post-scale + nearest-even produced a ~0.3% drift in token probabilities on our summarization slice, and a few runs showed Rouge-L regression in the 0.2-0.5% band for longctx prompts. not huge but visible for tight SLO customers.

michael: mitigation idea: pre-scale + per-channel scales on weight rows. that lowers bias but can be expensive if we must materialize a transposed copy. could we do a stride-aware fastpath to avoid copies for common shapes?

sara: my suggested defaults: runtime default = pre-scale + per-tensor nearest-even rounding. gated canary option = pre-scale + per-channel stochastic rounding for customers who opt in. also expose an explicit header flag so clients can request legacy post-scale semantics if they rely on exact int8 behaviour.

kevin: agree on header exposure. also: restrict stochastic rounding to hosted canary only by default; do not make it the platform-wide default since it affects reproducibility for experiments.

anya: operational nuance: if model metadata lacks per-channel scales, runtime should fall back to per-tensor path automatically and log a warning. we must avoid silent correctness mismatches.

michael: for implementation let's add a pre-scale per-channel fastpath that checks stride/alignment and avoids copies when dims line up. for the rare mismatched shape we can fall back to a buffered transpose. i'll prototype heuristics.

kevin: accumulation semantics: on fp8 paths use fp16 accumulation for matmuls; on int8 paths keep int32 accumulation. mixing accumulators causes dynamic range issues. document this in the runtime contract and in the API guidance.

anya: proposed test harness: run a small shadow harness that runs forward pass for 3x2x2 matrix: (pre/post scale) x (per-tensor/per-channel) x (nearest/stochastic) across 1k prompts. compute tokenwise logit diffs, KL on softmax inputs, and downstream evals. produce lightweight summary metrics for canary dashboards.

michael: i'll run microbenchmarks for the fastpath vs naive copy on A100 and L4 and capture p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput curves.

sara: sketching config header for runtime and clients:

```yaml
quant:
  profile: "fp8_default" # fp8_default | int8_legacy | mixed
  transpose_strategy: "pre_scale" # pre_scale | post_scale
  scaling:
    granularity: "per_tensor" # per_tensor | per_channel
    rounding: "nearest_even" # nearest_even | stochastic | bankers
  kv_metadata:
    boundary_index_header: "x-kv-precision-boundary-idx"
```

kevin: add note: rounding: stochastic only enabled during canary and must be explicitly requested in a canary header. do not enable in infra-wide defaults.

deploy-bot: canary-run started for quant-runtime branch - smoke tests executing :gear: (logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/10234)

anya: another gotcha: clients that switch precision mid-sequence (example: warmup tokens in fp16 then switch to fp8 for steady-state) must include a token-indexed handshake in the kv header. otherwise runtime and client will disagree on scaling and we will misread cached KV shards under longctx. propose `x-kv-precision-boundary-idx` as a non-opaque int marker. runtime returns 4xx + diagnostics if mismatch.

michael: good call. add validation: runtime asserts the boundary index matches cache metadata on load and refuses to use the cache if mismatch is detected; it should surface a clear error to the client and include diagnostics for traceback.

sara: action items/owners:
- anya: implement pre-scale per-channel fastpath + the comparison harness (owner)
- michael: perf microbench on A100/L4 and capture p50/p95/p99 (owner)
- kevin: write docs for accumulation semantics and rounding guidance (owner)
- sara: update RFC with these defaults, header contract, and canary gating plan (owner)

anya: i'll start a PR in repo/quant-runtime tomorrow with the harness.

michael: perf runs queued, will post results by EOD.

kevin: docs draft incoming, will ping for review once early draft is ready.

sara: thanks all. if canary smoke stays green i'll move the RFC status to `implementation_pending` and schedule a short sync with eng-infra for header validation wiring. :+1:

deploy-bot: canary-smoke passed; full regression running (link: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/10234).
